extracted.intended_audience: Legal scholars, practitioners, public officials, government employees, and potential guest contributors to the Yale Journal on Regulation's Notice & Comment blog
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting guest blog posts to the Yale Journal on Regulation's Notice & Comment blog, which publishes timely commentary on a wide range of regulatory topics and facilitates dialogue between scholars and practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic scope / subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The blog facilitates dialogue about a wide variety of regulatory topics including administrative law generally, financial regulation, corporate law, environmental law, bankruptcy law, and tax law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog takes a broad view of regulation and welcomes contributions from legal scholars and practitioners that may inform our understanding of public regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred contributors / authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: We regularly post guest submissions from legal scholars, public officials, government employees, and practitioners on a wide range of regulatory topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are expected from people working in or studying the field; the site is oriented toward the administrative law community (judges, lawyers, government officials, specialists in government relations, teachers and students of law).

rubrics_metrics.name: Student work policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We generally do not publish student work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student posts may be accepted only occasionally and only if of extraordinary quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use policy
rubrics_metrics.description: While we do not prohibit the use of AI in drafting blog posts, we regularly reject submissions where its use has clearly degraded the quality, originality, and/or credibility of the writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of AI is acceptable only so long as it does not harm quality, originality, or credibility; reviewers will screen for degraded writing attributable to AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method / contact
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit a guest post, or for more information on how to do so, please email jreg-blog@yale.edu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email is the required submission/contact route; reach out for submission details or questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship and organizational disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles published on Notice and Comment reflect the views of the individuals that prepared them, and do not necessarily represent the position of the American Bar Association, the Section of Administrative Law and Regulatory Practice, or the editors of Yale Journal on Regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors' opinions are personal; institutional endorsement should not be assumed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing policy and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a blog that publishes views in real time with light editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because publication is timely with light editing, errors can occur but can be promptly addressed by the post’s author; quick publication is prioritized over heavy copyediting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrasting views / openness to responses
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is a substantive disagreement, we welcome contrasting views and can publish those in real time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog encourages dialogue and may publish responses or differing perspectives quickly to facilitate conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation and sponsorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice & Comment is published jointly by the Yale Journal on Regulation and the American Bar Association Section of Administrative Law and Regulatory Practice, and it is sponsored by Davis Polk & Wardell LLP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog's institutional affiliations may inform its audience and standing but do not determine content endorsement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement / Section activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The ABA Section of Administrative Law and Regulatory Practice is a gathering place for those who work in administrative law and runs committees, webinars, conferences, a weekly blog, a quarterly journal, and other publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors and readers are encouraged to engage with the broader Section activities and committees; the blog is part of a wider professional community.
